messages:
Aisha Khan: Hi all, first day q: my kubectl keeps defaulting to namespace 'default' even after I set 'redwood-team'. I think my kubeconfig was merged from old guides. macOS, zsh. Anyone have a quick fix?

Tom Rivera: Welcome Aisha :wave: Quick wins: 1) create a named context that pins the namespace, 2) optionally remove ambiguous contexts. Show `kubectl config current-context` first.

Aisha Khan: current-context is `arn:aws:eks:us-west-2:222222222222:cluster/redwood-dev` and when I run `kubectl get pods` it shows pods from default.

Tom Rivera: Run these locally: `kubectl config set-context aisha-redwood --cluster=redwood-dev --user=arn:aws:eks:us-west-2:222222222222:exec --namespace=redwood-team` then `kubectl config use-context aisha-redwood`. That will pin the namespace so `kubectl get pods` uses redwood-team by default.

Aisha Khan: Ran that and `kubectl config current-context` shows `aisha-redwood`. `kubectl get pods` is now listing redwood-team pods. Thanks! Also got a 403 on describe earlier.

Tom Rivera: I just created a RoleBinding `redwood-team-view` giving your GH handle `aisha-k` view in namespace `redwood-team`. If you still see 403 run `kubectl auth can-i describe pods -n redwood-team`.

devex-bot: [system] rolebinding/redwood-team-view created by Tom Rivera at 2026-03-25T15:20:00Z

Aisha Khan: `kubectl auth can-i describe pods -n redwood-team` returns yes now. All good. I'll add the context pin step to my onboarding notes. Thanks :smile:
